主要内容: PG&E, a major California utility company, has reached a deal with its creditors over its restructuring plan. The creditors, led by Elliott Management and Pacific Investment Management Co, have agreed to drop their reorganization plan and support PG&E's proposal, pending approval by a bankruptcy court. The new notes under PG&E's plan are expected to save its customers about $1 billion. PG&E filed for Chapter 11 protection in January 2020, citing potential liabilities exceeding $30 billion from deadly wildfires in 2017 and 2018 linked to its equipment. The company also faced criticism for precautionary power outages last year due to the risk of wildfires. California Governor Gavin Newsom expressed his objection to the restructuring plan, stating that PG&E has not adequately addressed his concerns.
